title: Fliks plugin catalog submission (pluginApi 0)
description: One plugins/<id>/versions/<version>.json file. Every field is required by either the consumer's CatalogDocument parser (backend/src/modules/plugins/catalog/catalog.ts) or the install pipeline that reads a catalog version entry (backend/src/modules/plugins/plugin-install.service.ts). name/description/author/kind are plugin-level and must be identical across every version of the same id; the catalog carries one of each per plugin.

id.description: Reverse-DNS-style plugin id, e.g. "fliks.download". Required non-empty by CatalogPluginEntry.id.

name.description: Human-readable name. CatalogPluginEntry.name (any string, but the catalog gains nothing from an empty one).

kind.description: CatalogPluginEntry.kind — must match the PluginKind declared inside the signed plugin.json this version points to.

version.description: CatalogVersionEntry.version. Required non-empty; must be valid semver.

pluginApi.description: CatalogVersionEntry.pluginApi. Checked for exact equality against PLUGIN_API_VERSION (currently 0, see backend/src/common/plugin-contract/protocol.ts) at catalog, install and handshake time. Not itself required to equal 0 here — an old version entry legitimately keeps whatever pluginApi it shipped with.

fliks.description: CatalogVersionEntry.fliks — a semver range parsed with semver.validRange, and a mandatory upper bound (plan decision 16). e.g. ">=2.1.0 <3.0.0", never ">=2.1.0" alone.

zipUrl.description: Install-pipeline field read by plugin-install.service.ts's installFromCatalog (A1: GET <zipUrl>). Not read by parseCatalogDocument itself, but required for the entry to be installable.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex sha256 of the exact .fkplugin archive bytes at zipUrl. Checked (A2) against the downloaded bytes before any archive guard runs — this is the value that makes the catalog itself part of the trust chain, not just a directory.

logo.description: Display-only, read by the client's catalogue card (CatalogPlugin.logo). Absolute https URL: the card renders it before anything is installed, so a path inside the archive is unreachable.
